question: 100 prisoners each open 50 of 100 boxes to find their own number; all must succeed. With the best strategy, what's the chance?
answer: About 31%. Each prisoner opens the box with their own number, then the box named inside it, and so on round a loop. All succeed exactly when no loop of boxes is longer than 50, which happens about 31% of the time. Opening boxes at random would give (½)¹⁰⁰: effectively nothing.
move: Coordinated choices can succeed where independent ones almost surely fail.
ask: Where could my group coordinate instead of each of us guessing alone?
trap: Almost zero, multiplying a hundred coin flips together.
source: Gál and Miltersen, The cell probe complexity of succinct data structures, 2003
reference: Anna Gál and Peter Bro Miltersen, The Cell Probe Complexity of Succinct Data Structures, ICALP, 2003
